title: GTM CS 1:1 prep - Samira Patel / Nora Wu - 2026-03-29
content:
Purpose:
- Quick sync ahead of renewal conversation for Acorn Health (renewal due 2026-04-15).
- Surface risks, agree on ask (discount, exec intro, timeline), align on next steps and owners.

Agenda (30m):
1) Quick personal check-in (2-3m)
2) Account health snapshot (5m) — recent usage, support volume, NPS pulse
3) Renewal posture + risks (10m) — pricing, feature asks, decision timeline
4) Asks and internal blockers (5m) — legal, SSO, training credits
5) Next steps + owners (5m)

Notes / context (things to have on hand):
- ARR ~ $120k, current monthly usage trending down ~12% last 6 wks (tokens/day drop off after pilot).
- Primary contacts: Nora (CS), Miguel (AE), executive sponsor: CTO - Lina Park.
- Open tickets: CS-4121 (SSO config blocking org-wide rollout), CS-4189 (prompt latency on private deployment).
- Last meeting 2026-03-10: committed to internal pilot expansion, asked for training session w/eng team — scheduled 2026-03-31 (hold?).
- Value props we should emphasize: predictable latency, cost controls (Redwood Optimize suggestions), private deployment options for PHI.

Key risks / signals:
- Usage drop suggests pilot not expanding — need to confirm whether it's product fit or operations friction.
- Legal procurement timeline looks long (Procurement says 4-6 weeks for standard SOW) — might affect renewal.
- SSO ticket (CS-4121) blocks org-wide rollout; engineering estimate low effort but needs sign-off from infra team (we should escalate).

Talking points / questions to Nora to surface in 1:1:
- How aligned are AE/Miguel + exec sponsor on the rollout timeline? Any pushback from Lina?
- Do we have a clear list of features that would move them from pilot -> production? (SSO, role-based access, audit logs?)
- Is the usage drop localized to a team or across the org? Any qualitative feedback from power users?
- Is procurement the main gating factor vs. technical blockers?
- Would they accept a short-term extension or phased renewal (pay-for-prod seats only) if procurement takes longer?

Proposed ask for renewal meeting with customer:
- Short-term: offer 45-day extension with standard terms, waive onboarding fee, schedule 2 training sessions for eng+security (value-add).
- Long-term: commit to a pilot-to-production plan with milestones (SSO resolved, security review passed, 2 teams onboarded).
- Ask AE to introduce Lina to product exec for faster sign-off if procurement stalls.

Internal blockers I can help with:
- Escalate CS-4121 to infra lead (pinged Max Evans already).
- Prepare one-pager on security posture + SOC/KMS details to speed security approval (I can draft).
- Draft renewal extension language for legal to review (2-3 business days).

Action items (owner, due):
- Samira: Draft security one-pager and export usage metrics for last 90d (due 2026-03-30).
- Nora: Confirm exec alignment and whether Lina will join renewal call (due 2026-03-31).
- Max Evans: Triage CS-4121 with infra and provide ETA for SSO config (due 2026-03-27).
- Miguel (AE): Prep renewal proposal and optional phased pricing (due 2026-04-01).

Open questions / TODOs:
- If infra ETA slips >10 days, do we propose a temporary workaround (manual invite flow + audit log) or push for extension?
- Confirm whether training sessions need to be recorded / hosted by Solutions Eng or self-serve.

Misc scratch notes (phrases I might use):
- "We want to keep momentum — a small extension gives procurement breathing room and keeps your pilots intact."
- "We can prioritize SSO as part of a production cutover plan — our infra team is ready to collaborate."

Links to bring:
- Usage dashboard (internal): https://dash.redwood.internal/acorn-health/usage (ask Nora to grant me viewer if not accessible)
- Confluence: CUST-Playbook-123 (security checklist)
- JIRA tickets: CS-4121, CS-4189

Post-meeting follow-up template (I'll send):
- Summary of decisions, agreed extension term (if any), owners + deadlines, next meeting date.

Quick personal notes for catch-up:
- Nora recently back from parental leave — ask about bandwidth and best meeting times.
- Keep tone collaborative; they like straightforward, low-ops solutions.


-- end of prep doc --

(Working / rough — will tidy after 1:1 and copy final follow-up to Confluence.)
